question: A team is writing the instructions for a shared project that will be used for all of its customer communications. Which direction belongs in the project instructions rather than in an individual chat?
options: A) Summarise the complaint from the Ashworth account that came in during yesterday afternoon.
B) Write at a reading level suited to customers, and never quote internal ticket references.
C) Draft this week's outage notice, keeping it to one paragraph for the status page.
D) Compare the two apology drafts below and say which reads better for this customer.
correct_answers: B) Write at a reading level suited to customers, and never quote internal ticket references.
explanations: This is a one-off task tied to a single conversation, not standing direction for the project.
Correct. Project instructions carry durable, project-wide direction such as tone, audience and house rules, so they apply consistently to every chat in the project.
A specific deliverable for this week belongs in the chat where it is being produced.
A request about material pasted into one conversation cannot serve as project-wide direction.
